key_insight: Zero-shot compositional action models often learn an object-driven shortcut—predicting verbs from objects—because compositional supervision is sparse/skewed and verbs are learned asymmetrically; mitigating this disentanglement failure substantially improves generalization to unseen verb–object pairs.
problem_solved: Addresses poor zero-shot generalization in Compositional Video Understanding by identifying and mitigating an overlooked failure mode: object-driven verb shortcuts that cause models to fail on novel verb–object combinations.
method: Systematic diagnosis: quantify shortcut behavior via per-composition sparsity/skew analyses and error attribution showing verbs dominated by object cues.

Training-time mitigation: apply disentangling strategies (e.g., balanced reweighting, compositional augmentation, and contrastive/object-agnostic regularization) to reduce object→verb shortcut learning.
Evaluation: measure zero-shot compositional performance and robustness across benchmarks to validate improved generalization to unseen verb–object pairs.
impact: Provides a practical path to reduce shortcut-driven failures in video action recognition, improving robustness and real-world generalization for systems that must compose verbs and objects they haven't seen together.
visual_elements: Heatmap/confusion matrix highlighting verbs predicted from objects (showing object-driven shortcut errors).
Bar chart comparing zero-shot accuracy before vs. after mitigation for seen/unseen compositions.
Schematic pipeline diagram: diagnosis → disentangling interventions (reweighting/augmentation/contrastive) → improved inference.
t-SNE or feature-space visualization showing reduced entanglement between object and verb representations after mitigation.
paper_title: Why Can't I Open My Drawer? Mitigating Object-Driven Shortcuts in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Inwoong Lee, Taeoh Kim, Minho Shim, Dongyoon Wee
